Full fund list is in the source PDF if wanted later.
_meta.confidence: High -- transcribed directly from the district's own published, adopted budget document. Function totals reconciled exactly against the district's own General Fund total ($7,679,054).

budget_message_highlights: General Fund resource totals: 2021-22 $7,821,367 (audited), 2022-23 $8,164,371 (audited), 2023-24 $8,487,264 (audited), 2024-25 $7,672,884 (budgeted), 2025-26 $7,679,054 (adopted) -- a declining trend after peaking in 2023-24.

Direct quote from the district's own budget message: 'Declining enrollment coupled with a decrease in the teacher experience adjustment is negatively impacting our state funding. The district continues to receive more funds from property taxes than the state school fund.' -- this directly confirms and illustrates the enrollment-based funding mechanism explained elsewhere in this project.
The State School Fund projection this budget was built on: $11.359 billion of statewide education funding for the 2025-27 biennium, split 49/51 between the two years.
There are no wage increases built into the 2025-26 budget; expenditures were cut across the general fund, with no funds for textbook adoption or classroom furniture this year.
The district is still spending down a May 2023 voter-approved bond for facility projects, expected substantially complete by fall 2025.

app_display_guidance.suggested_grouping: Instruction vs. Support Services vs. Other is a standard, recognizable framing in education finance -- consider using it as the primary breakdown, with the individual programs (elementary instruction, transportation, plant operations, etc.) as a drill-down within each.
app_display_guidance.good_pull_quote_for_app: Central Curry's own budget message says it plainly: enrollment decline and a lower teacher-experience adjustment are hurting state funding, and the district now gets more from local property taxes than from the State School Fund -- a real, current example of the enrollment-funding mechanism explained elsewhere in this app.
app_display_guidance.biggest_single_program: Office of the Principal (school-level administration) is the single largest support-services line at $725,750 -- larger than technology, transportation, or fiscal services individually. Operation & Maintenance of Plant ($961,259) is the single largest support line overall.
